### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via os migrate stored-references (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-references/index.ts))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/email-service.mdx`  _(via callerPackageId (symbol, a field of interface ArtifactDatasetResolution))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via os migrate stored-references (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-references/index.ts))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via validateWidgetBindings (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via validateWidgetBindings (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **189** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bf02d33bd64f496aa8166e1a235ef10977927947` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bf777636dce09b39659ce56e74fb43685fb38be1` — the merge of head `e29910fcd7d60f1cab7158c3828ac7402ba29c62` into base `bf02d33bd64f496aa8166e1a235ef10977927947`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bf777636dce09b39659ce56e74fb43685fb38be1 && git checkout bf777636dce09b39659ce56e74fb43685fb38be1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bf02d33bd64f496aa8166e1a235ef10977927947 e29910fcd7d60f1cab7158c3828ac7402ba29c62 && git checkout -B drift-repro bf02d33bd64f496aa8166e1a235ef10977927947 && git merge --no-ff e29910fcd7d60f1cab7158c3828ac7402ba29c62

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bf02d33bd64f496aa8166e1a235ef10977927947
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bf02d33bd64f496aa8166e1a235ef10977927947` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/lint/src/validate-widget-bindings.ts`. On the per-package pass the walk is the runtime's rule (`resolvePackageScopedHolders`): the package's own dataset first, then the one holder inside `packageResolutionClosure`, whatever is held outside it; two inside refuse and nothing is picked; none inside refuses naming every holder. `sys` bodies are in reach by `namespace`, and the registry handed to the walk has the shape `picklist-references.ts` hands it. The wording picks the fix from the artifact (a holder whose own closure reaches the reader is never offered as a dependency), which is what the card asks. Two cases fall outside that (M2, S1) and one neighbour moves unsaid (N1).

`packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts`. Sentence branches only: environment-only names the move alone, two or more package holders ask for one dependency, the one-holder sentence is unchanged. Both new branches are pinned.

`packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.ts`, `stored-package-references.ts`, `commands/migrate/stored-references/index.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts`. The carried nits of 6841428662, as sentences; the picklist hint's cycle arm reads the artifact and is pinned.

`packages/qa/dogfood/test/dataset-app-reads-module.dogfood.test.ts`. The card's three cells on real doors. Not run here.

Findings:

- **M1 must-fix. The kind is `narrowed`.** AGENTS.md: "a value refused or a requirement tightened is `narrowed`", and the kind is "the change to what a metadata author can write". After this diff an author can no longer build a package dashboard whose widget names a dataset that only an undeclared package of the artifact holds: `os build` and `os validate` exit 1 where they exited 0. That the runtime refused the READ since 18.4.0 does not make it `none`: no door refused the metadata until this one. Precedent, counted in `packages/lint/CHANGELOG.md` over the entries that carry a narrowing arm and a kind: 57 `narrowed`, 1 `semantic`, 5 `none`. Of the five, two are runtime doors that take no metadata (769adff, f57eddc), two are doors joining a refusal `os build` and `os validate` already made (c133cfe, 7f368f5), and one reads the other way (9127f23, an email template's hole placements, citing ruling A). The 57 include the publish door refusing a widget `filter` key on a dataset outside the package's closure, and the nearest sibling on `main`, `.changeset/32978-define-stack-packages-single-app.md`, is `narrowed`, `minor`, registered. Owed: `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` in the PR body and the changeset, `minor` on `@objectstack/lint` at least, an `adr-0087: registered` ledger entry (the upgrade guide is where an author upgrading a multi-package artifact learns of the refusal before `os build` makes it), and the BREAKING banner. The card's own dispatch line says `none`, so the seat corrects it there too. This is derived from the rule text and the weight of precedent; a maintainer ruling that an authoring refusal of this kind is outside the protocol, cited in the PR, would settle it the other way.
- **M2 must-fix. The union run is not left as it was for a stack that keeps a top-level `datasets`.** Derived from the code, not run. The per-package pass is recognised by `stack.manifest.id` naming one of the bodies. The union run of a `composeStacks(…, { manifest: 'preserve' })` artifact meets that test too: its manifest is the last input's (`selectManifest(…, 'last')`), whose body is in `packages[]`. It stays unchanged only because `authoringRuleUnionStack` folds every body's datasets onto the top level, and that fold skips a key the top level already carries. So for a `packages[]` stack with a top-level `datasets` of its own (the residual ADR-0130 D4 registers under `manifest.id`) and no top-level `dashboards`, the folded dashboards of every package are judged as the manifest package's: a module's dashboard on the module's OWN dataset is refused `outside-closure`, with a sentence saying the installed read answers 409, when the module is outside that package's closure (HotCRM's shape, the module depending on the app). `main` accepts that stack and the runtime serves the read. The docblock and the pin describe a union whose manifest "is none of its bodies" (`com.example.suite`), which is not the union the doors hand the rule. Owed: recognise the per-package pass by more than the id (it hands the body itself as `manifest`), or leave the union run on the every-body read; and a pin on the shape the doors really produce, with a residual dataset.
- **S1 should-fix. A dependency the artifact does not carry.** `picklist-references.ts`, the reading this walk says it follows, reports instead of refusing when the declaring package names a dependency outside the artifact, because that package may hold the name (its header, "Declared dependencies outside the stack: reported, never refused"). This walk refuses, and its message states as fact that the installed read answers 409. When the reader declares such a dependency and that package holds the name, the runtime resolves it there and serves it. Take the twin's arm, or say in the message that holders outside the artifact are not read.
- **N1 nit.** `validate-report-runtime-filter.ts` reads the same index, so on the per-package pass a report's `runtimeFilter` on a refused name is no longer judged. No verdict is lost (`chart-dataset-unknown` already refuses that report there, and the union run still judges the filter), but the FROM/TO table speaks of widgets only.
